concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i < x.length - 1; i++) x[i] = x[i + 1];
concepts.why: The code uses the loop variable as the index, so x[i] and x[i+1] reach new elements on each pass. The bound x.length - 1 keeps x[i+1] inside 0..length-1. A left rotation is a familiar variant, so this is relational rather than L4.

concepts.quote: int first = x[0]; for (int i = 0; i < x.length - 1; i++) x[i] = x[i + 1]; x[x.length - 1] = first;
concepts.why: Saving x[0] first and stepping the index upward, the opposite of the original downward loop, makes a correct left shift. Adapting the given code to a familiar variant counts only as relational.
i++ is used correctly as the usual for-loop update, adding 1 to the index on each pass.
The header correctly packages the start value, the guard and the update, so i covers 0..length-2 for the shift. The new code adapts a familiar pattern, so it is relational rather than L4.
